# Owner decisions (2026-11-07): PF-0047 Runtime Manager and PF-0048 New Project Wizard

I explicitly approve the proposed directions for PF-0047 (Development Runtime Manager) and PF-0048 (New Project Wizard), subject to the following requirements.

## PF-0047 — Runtime Manager

1. Loopback port checks: Approved. Allow narrowly scoped checks against 127.0.0.1 for explicitly configured project service ports, with strict timeouts. Do not weaken the general prohibition against arbitrary network access or introduce external network probing.
2. Services surviving Console shutdown: Approved. Local development services may continue running after the browser or Console closes. However, YallaFlow must track ownership safely across restarts. Only stop processes that it can positively identify as belonging to the managed project. If ownership cannot be established, report the process as unmanaged instead of terminating it.
3. Personal command trust: Approved. Trust decisions must remain local and git-ignored, bound to the effective command, working directory and relevant runtime configuration. Any material command or configuration change requires renewed confirmation. Never automatically execute commands inferred from repository files without review.
4. Controlled execution environment: Approved. Use a minimal, well-defined base environment plus explicitly configured variables. Do not automatically inherit credentials, tokens, secrets, or sensitive environment variables.

Additional requirements: support Start, Stop, Restart, Status and Logs; distinguish running, stopped, failed, starting and unknown states accurately; never stop unrelated services or processes; do not automatically start services when opening a project; use the approved shared runtime configuration with safe local overrides; preserve command trust, process lifecycle, logging and error handling across Console restarts; include security, crash-recovery and concurrency tests.

## PF-0048 — New Project Wizard

I approve treating projects created from an explicitly selected, trusted generator through YallaFlow's Wizard as Greenfield projects. Requirements:
1. The Wizard must create a genuinely new project in a validated target location.
2. Never overwrite an existing repository or silently classify an existing project as Greenfield.
3. Record generator/template provenance and the selected technology stack.
4. Do not treat generated code as fully understood or its architecture as approved.
5. Keep existing-project discovery and baseline approval rules intact.
6. Show the selected stack, generated structure and commands before executing them.
7. Require confirmation for scaffolding operations that execute external commands or install dependencies.
8. Handle generator failures and partial creation safely, preserving useful diagnostics.
9. Initialize YallaFlow using the canonical Core.
10. Allow the user to continue with Claude Code or Codex using the normal workflow and subscription-based integration.

## Execution authorization

Record these as my explicit product and specification decisions. Update the PF-0047 and PF-0048 specifications to reflect these constraints. Preserve YallaFlow's actual approval history; do not invent approval of a plan that I have not reviewed. Proceed with all work already authorized under these decisions. If a new specification or plan gate still requires a separate explicit approval, leave that gate pending and continue any other independent work. Complete both milestones as far as the authorized scope permits, including implementation, focused tests, browser testing, independent security reviews and documentation. Then prepare the final integration and stabilization work for v1.4.0. Continue only in /home/engamer/Amasi/YallaFlow-1.4 on feature/workspace-1.4; push verified development commits there. Do not merge conflicting YallaFlow work histories, alter production projects, merge to main, tag, release or publish. Target: one complete v1.4.0 acceptance candidate (Work Lifecycle, Console Work Management, Project Overview and onboarding, Development Runtime Manager, New Project Wizard). Stop only for genuinely new owner decisions, security exceptions or approval gates that remain mandatory.
